# Mohith Rai Srivastav

> Architectural photographer, filmmaker, and educator based in Goa, India. Architect by education, photographer by practice.

## About

Mohith Rai Srivastav translates the built environment through a practice of slowness, materiality, and sustained attention. His work spans architectural photography, slow cinema, and fine art prints. He is based in Goa, India, working across India and open to commissions worldwide.

## What This Site Offers

### Fine Art Prints (Shop)
Limited-edition archival pigment prints on 310 GSM etching rag, dry mounted on museum-grade humidity-resistant board, in a slim matte black frame with glass. Unframed is available on request. Each print is signed on the back, numbered, and accompanied by a certificate of authenticity. Nine works are currently available, from the Resurface series, each in one edition size: INR 85,000 (edition of 5 + 1 AP), or INR 1,25,000 for Cosmic Return (edition of 2 + 1 AP). Prints are final sale. They ship worldwide, fully insured, and crating and shipping are quoted per order. The shop includes an augmented reality (AR) preview, so buyers can place a print on their wall using their phone camera before purchasing.

### The Explorer's Deck — Architecture and Design Edition (Shop)
A creative observation deck of 63 cards across seven lenses: Sensation, Line & Direction, Colour & Value, Rhythm & Balance, Use & Behaviour, Form & Scale, and Wild. First Edition. Each card has three parts: a Mission (a specific task), a Key (a question that sharpens focus), and a Why (the idea behind the task). Use it solo, with a group, or in a workshop. Pick a place. Draw a card. See what it surfaces. Price: INR 2,100 (incl. all taxes). Ships worldwide. Available now at https://www.mohithraisrivastav.com/shop.html. Full deck details: https://www.mohithraisrivastav.com/explorers-deck.html. Used in every Lived Space workshop session. For designers, architects, photographers, writers, students, creative groups, design schools, museums, and anyone training perception or attention.

### Resurface (Photographic Series)
An ongoing photographic enquiry into how the built world remains active through surface, erosion, and light. Each chapter explores different material conditions, climates, and qualities of light. Chapter I was exhibited at the Goa Open Arts Festival 2026. Editions are sold framed, with glass.

### Creative Workshops — Lived Space
A hands-on creative observation workshop based in Goa, India — and available on invitation nationwide and internationally. The workshop places observation first — participants spend time in the field noticing people, routines, and sensory detail, then take a single constraint and respond in their own medium. The practice changes how you choose and what you make. Institutions, design schools, festivals, and organizations can invite Lived Space to their city.

**Method:** Three repeatable steps — (1) Observe: no camera, no notebook, just look. (2) Constrain: one card, one instruction, work inside it completely. (3) Make: one response in your medium. The depth comes from how you apply them.

**Open to:** Photographers, architects, writers, filmmakers, musicians, designers — any creative discipline. Beginner to professional. No prior experience required.

**Formats:**
- The One-Day Immersion — 6 to 8 hours, one completed work in your medium. INR 3,900 + GST. 2026–2027 dates: 13 July 2026, 9 August 2026, 2 September 2026, 9 November 2026, 5 December 2026, 1 February 2027, 3 March 2027.
- The Three-Day Intensive — The same space, returned to across three days. Each session follows the three steps. Two group reviews and one personal mentoring conversation are included. INR 11,400 + GST. 2026–2027 start dates: 20 July 2026, 5 August 2026, 4 September 2026, 11 November 2026, 6 December 2026, 3 February 2027, 5 March 2027.
- The Six-Day Residency — A six-day creative residency closing with one finished work. INR 23,000 + GST. 2026–2027 start dates: 1 October 2026, 9 January 2027, 1 April 2027.
- All sessions held in Goa, India. Group size 12 to 15.

**Includes:** All workshop sessions, Explorer's Deck (constraint cards), field guidance during observation, group review after every session.
**Not included:** Travel, accommodation, meals, personal equipment.
**What to bring:** Your medium, comfortable clothing for extended time outdoors, a willingness to observe before you make.

### Teaching & Institutional Engagements

Mohith Rai Srivastav works as a Workshop Tutor and educator at architecture schools, student conventions, and creative institutions across India.

**Institutional Record:**
- NASA India — 68th Annual Convention (June 2026): Invited to conduct Lived Space: Creative Observation at Woxsen School of Architecture & Planning, Hyderabad. NASA India is the National Association of Students of Architecture, representing 66,000 students across 350+ colleges.
- CARE School of Architecture, Trichy (2024): Workshop on Photography as a Tool for Architects, co-facilitated with Bharath Ramamrutham.
- ASTU-AAS Webinar (2023): Architectural Photography — Discussion & Insight, hosted by the Association of Architecture Students, Adama Science and Technology University, Ethiopia. International engagement.

### Architectural Photography Services
Available for architectural documentation, editorial work, and bespoke print commissions. Portfolio spans residential, institutional, heritage, hospitality, and industrial projects across India, including Goa, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Sanand (Gujarat), and Sawantwadi (Maharashtra). Based in Goa, India, working across India and open to commissions worldwide.

### Fine Art & Exhibitions
Mohith's work sits at the intersection of architecture and fine art. He is open to gallery exhibitions, art residencies, museum shows, art fairs, and curatorial collaborations. Previous exhibition: Goa Open Arts Festival 2026. Available for artist residencies, group and solo exhibitions, and commissioned installations for public and private spaces.

### Journal & Essays
Long-form essays on architectural photography, light, time, observation, materiality, and the gap between what architects draw and what people experience. Written from years of working inside finished buildings across India.

**Currently published:**
- "What Architectural Photography Taught Me About Space" (May 2026) — On planning a shoot around the sun path, what changes between the recce and the shoot day, and what years of photographing finished buildings has taught about light, time, use, and the gap between what is drawn and what is experienced. https://www.mohithraisrivastav.com/what-architectural-photography-taught-me-about-space.html

The full journal index lives at https://www.mohithraisrivastav.com/blog.html and updates with new field notes and essays.
